title: Pay with Hampton, Basie and Lloyd Price
summary: Nightly wages, hotel and meals paid by sidemen.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Yeah. What kind of, we talked about how you changed band to band, you got better pay. What kind of pay were you getting in those days? What was a good salary in those days?

Well, I'm ashamed to say it, but at that time the money wasn't like it is now. When I first went away with Lionel Hampton, I was making nineteen dollars a night. Now that nineteen dollars, if you just work one week, I mean one night, you just got nineteen dollars. Then, after I left, I started, when I came back, I was making about twenty-five. For a night? Yeah. For a night, yeah. Yeah. Now when I first went away with Basie, that was the most money I made with a big band. I was getting three hundred dollars a week. And I'm-
Now who paid the hotel? We had to pay the hotel.
We had to pay everything. Now when I went with Lloyd Price, I was getting twenty dollars a night. Two hundred dollars a night. Again, you had to pick up the hotel?
That's right. And your meals? And your meals?

That's right. The only thing we didn't have to pay was, but see, Buddy Richen, that's a guy, a little white dude named Don Rader, he was good, good trumpet player. He left Woody Harman, I know he left Woody Harman band to come with us. And he said, man, shit, I wish I had known that Basie was paying this kind of money. I would have been over here, man. He said, we didn't get, we were getting thirteen or fourteen dollars a night with Buddy Rich. And another guy who left staying kitten bands, a white guy, he came with Basie after leaving staying kitten. And he said, man, I never did get, and he was just getting two hundred dollars a week. He said, man, I never did get this kind of money with staying kitten. See, now like what staying kitten, a lot of happens to most of those guys, they get those young guys out of school who can play. These guys will play for nothing. They just want to get out there and play and make a name for themselves.
What about, okay, so you had transportation they paid for, but you had meals, hotel, what about your laundry? I mean you had a suit every night, right? No, not the uniform.

A uniform. Yeah, well now, and- Who paid for the pressing? Now the first time, when I first got with a lot of happens, we had to pay for that too. They were sending to the cleaners. They were sending. Yeah, but you had to pay for it, deduct that out your salary. But see, we didn't know. We thought we was doing something big, you know. Because that was something, you know, to play with a big band. Like a lot of those guys I play with now, the young guys in their twenties, man, y'all played for that. Man, I never would have gone over there for that kind of money. I say if you had to come up during that time, you would have gone. You would be glad to get there. Because the musicians who stayed home, they didn't get any experience. They just played among themselves. And they were getting eight dollars a night.
